beats.care: If anyone asks you for money to 'get' you a job, walk away and report it. Real hiring doesn't work that way.
beats.what: Chennai airport police arrested a 52-year-old former Airports Authority of India official, accused of taking ₹1–2 lakh each from 12 job seekers.
beats.why: She allegedly promised well-paid airport jobs. Months passed with no appointments, and she allegedly went into hiding.

cards.body: Victims complained to the South Chennai Joint Commissioner of Police, and a special team traced her.
cards.caption: allegedly taken from 12 people

cards.body: Investigators reportedly found she had taken money on similar promises while still in service, and AAI had earlier held a departmental inquiry against her.

opts: The job was at an airport
Being asked to pay money to get a job
cards.q: What's the biggest red flag in this case?
cards.why: Paying someone to secure a job for you is the classic sign of a job scam.

cards.q: Ever been offered a job for a fee?

hook: Would you pay *₹2 lakh for an airport job*? 12 people did.

learn.t: Each person allegedly paid ₹1–2 lakh and got only a 'job application form' in return.

sources.name: DT Next
sources.title: Former Chennai airport official held for cheating 12 people of Rs 23 lakh

tldr: Chennai police arrested a retired airport official accused of taking ₹23 lakh from 12 young people for airport jobs that never came.
